intro_html: Thai green curry is built the proper way here, which means the paste gets fried in the thick cream at the top of the coconut milk can until the oil breaks out and the kitchen smells like a Bangkok side street. That one step separates a real curry from a can of soup with chicken in it. Eggplant, snow peas and a fistful of basil go in at the end. Each bowl runs 608 calories and 26 grams of protein for about $2.46.
cost_closing_html: About $2.46 a bowl. Coconut milk, fresh basil and curry paste are the three lines that set this price, and all three are exactly what makes it taste like the restaurant version instead of a shortcut.
shop_smart: Curry paste is the flavor engine and it is worth buying the real thing. If your store carries green paste, grab it. If it only stocks red, the jars we track work fine and nobody at your table will file a complaint.
Coconut milk is the biggest line. Buy full fat store brand cans, never light, and do not shake the can. You want the thick cream at the top for frying the paste, which is the whole technique.
Fresh basil is expensive by weight no matter where you buy it. A pot of living basil from the produce section costs about what two clamshells do and keeps producing on a windowsill for weeks.
Snow peas and eggplant go in at the very end. Buy them the day you cook, and if snow peas are priced like a luxury that week, frozen green beans slot right in without hurting anything.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Open the coconut milk cans without shaking them and spoon the thick cream off the top into your largest pot. Reserve the thin liquid underneath.
Heat the pot over medium-high and cook that coconut cream with the vegetable oil for 3 to 5 minutes until it splits and you can see clear oil pooling.

Add the curry paste, minced garlic, grated ginger and lemongrass paste and fry them in that oil for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens and smells sharp and fragrant. This is the step people skip and it is the one that matters.
Add the chicken thighs cut into strips and turn them in the paste for 3 minutes, then pour in the reserved coconut liquid and the chicken broth.
Add the cubed eggplant and simmer uncovered 15 to 20 minutes until the eggplant is soft and the sauce has reduced and thickened.
Season with the fish sauce, sugar, salt and black pepper, then add the snow peas and cook 2 minutes so they stay bright and snappy.
Kill the heat and stir in the lime juice, the fresh basil and the thin-sliced onion. Cook the rice separately and fold it in, or hold it in the containers underneath.
portion_html: Set the pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight, and divide by 14. Same scoop, fourteen times. Each one carries 608 calories, and reheat coconut curries at half power so the sauce stays emulsified instead of turning grainy.
upsell_html: Real Thai green curry, paste fried in coconut cream and all, for about $2.46 a bowl. This is one of a few hundred recipes on the site. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

steps: Spoon the thick cream off the coconut milk cans and fry it with oil until it splits and the oil pools.
Fry the curry paste, garlic, ginger and lemongrass in that oil for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken, then the reserved coconut liquid, broth and cubed eggplant, and simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and sugar, add the snow peas, and cook 2 minutes.
Finish off the heat with lime juice, basil and sliced onion, then portion into 14 containers with rice.
